title: POC scoping - Meridian Labs integration planning
summary: Redwood AE + SE and Meridian Labs engineering team scoped a 6-week POC focused on integration with Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, and structured JSON outputs. Discussed workload sizing (peak 40 rps inference, avg 12 rps), latency SLOs (p95 < 300ms for short prompts), cost targets, benchmark plan, SDKs (Python/Node) and security requirements (SAML, KMS). Agreed next steps: exchange sample payloads, schedule bench run (week of 4/6), provide security docs, and draft pilot contract.
topics: function/tool calling and structured output (JSON schema)
security and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-30 07:45 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Jordan Kim, Priya Rao (Redwood); Alicia Gomez, Ben Carter, Samir Patel (Meridian Labs)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): scoped poc, bench, SDKs, security yes/no.

Topics: success criteria, workloads, SDKs, function calling, structured output.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. we also have Priya, our SE. Alicia can you give a quick intro to the team?
00:28 Alicia: Yeah hi, Alicia here, CTO at Meridian Labs. Ben is our ML lead, Samir handles infra. We're looking to integrate LLM-based extraction into our research portal, um so interested in low lat and predictable cost.
00:55 Ben: Quick context — our traffic is bursty, daytime loads peak around experiment release cycles. Typical inference is 2-3 short prompts per research doc, average tokens small, but some long form summarization at night. We expect peak ~40 requests per second during bursts, avg ~12 rps overall.
01:30 Priya: Got it. that matches many customers. for the POC are you focused on hosted API or private / VPC?
01:55 Samir: Security is important. We prefer VPC peering or private deployment if possible, but open to hosted if we can get egress controls and KMS.
02:20 Jordan: Great — POC approach we suggested in the invite was 6 weeks: week 0 prep, weeks 1-2 bench + integration, weeks 3-4 evaluation and quality tuning, week 5-6 pilot wrap and handoff. Is that timeline realistic for you?
02:50 Alicia: Sounds reasonable. our internal stakeholders want p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts, and cost per 1k tokens less than $X — uh we'll put a number in the doc. main success criteria are latency, throughput, and extraction accuracy.
03:20 Priya: For accuracy, do you have a specific metric? e.g., F1 on entity extraction, exact match on structured JSON fields?
03:40 Ben: Yeah we can do F1 for named entities and a schema match for structured outputs; we'll generate a labeled set of ~500 examples.
04:05 Jordan: Great. Benchmarks: we'll run synthetic and real prompt runs. synthetic will exercise throughput/latency across sequence lengths. real prompt runs use your 500 labeled examples to measure quality and end-to-end latency. We typically expect hosting variation; if you want predictable latency we can propose Redwood Dedicated or private deployment.
05:00 Ben: Can you share the OpenAI-compatible endpoint? our stack already uses the OpenAI SDK wrappers.
05:20 Priya: Yes — Redwood exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints and native SDKs for Python and Node. you can swap the endpoint with minimal code changes. Note: function/tool calling is supported, but behavior has slight differences across models — we'll provide examples.
05:50 Samir: How do you handle structured output? we need strict JSON outputs validated against schema, sometimes with nested arrays.
06:10 Priya: We have a structured output feature — we can enforce JSON-only responses using a schema hinting approach and function-calling style. in practice we recommend using the function calling + post-parse validation for the strictest results; we also provide heuristics and a small reranker to increase exact match.
06:40 Ben: Any sample code?
06:45 Priya: I'll drop a sample repo link in the follow-up. it's minimal: replace the base URL to redwood API, add an api key, call as you would to OpenAI, example for function calling included.
07:05 Jordan: Security check — you mentioned KMS and SAML. we support KMS for private deployments and support SAML SSO and SSO provisioning. for hosted customers we have SOC2 and we can provide audit logs. do you have any specific compliance needs?
07:35 Alicia: We're under research confidentiality, need audit logs and data retention controls. SOC2 is a big check, plus ability to opt-out of retention for specific datasets.
08:00 Jordan: Understood. We'll include the security pack (SOC2 summary, data retention options, KMS notes).
08:18 Ben: For benchmarking, what's the runner? do you provide a harness or do we run locally?
08:30 Priya: We provide a bench harness (python-based), and instructions to run in your environment or ours. For private VPC deployments we run bench traffic from within the same VPC to measure true network latencies. For hosted we'll run from multiple regions to show variation.
09:00 Samir: Network wise, we'll need egress rules if hosted. if private, we'll coordinate peering. I'll surface firewall egress ports.
09:20 Jordan: Perfect. Let's talk specifics of integration: you said you already use OpenAI SDKs — so the minimal change is to swap endpoint and credentials. If you want function calling, we recommend using the OpenAI-compatible function calling endpoints. If you want a more resilient setup, Redwood supports tool calling via structured endpoints and fallback policies.
10:00 Ben: About cost — can you give a rough estimate for the POC?
10:10 Jordan: We can put together a POC pricing worksheet — it will include hosted usage estimate and a dedicated node estimate if you want predictable SLOs. For your expected peak/avg: we'll model token counts and run cost scenarios.
10:35 Alicia: Important: acceptance criteria must include both quantitative (p95 latency, F1 > 0.9 on extraction) and qualitative (no major regressions in developer experience).
11:00 Priya: Noted. For sample payloads, send us the prompt shapes and we'll create example curl commands and SDK snippets. Also we suggest you try both our Python SDK and direct OpenAI-compatible calls to test behavior parity.
11:30 Ben: Any caveats around streaming vs non-streaming? we might want streaming for long summaries.
11:40 Priya: Streaming is supported; it affects latency metrics (time-to-first-byte) vs total completion time. For summaries we can stream tokens; for structured extraction you typically want non-streamed to ensure full JSON integrity.
12:10 Jordan: Bench design: we'll run three profiles — short prompt low latency (50-200 tokens), medium prompt (200-800 tokens), and long summarization (1k+ tokens). for each profile we'll measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and exact-match on schema. Does that capture it?
12:45 Ben: Yes. Also measure cold vs warm cache. we have many repeated prefixes across docs; prefix caching could help.
13:05 Priya: Good call — we'll instrument for KV cache warmup. Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching; we'll include a test where we pre-warm with a corpus to simulate your real workload.
13:35 Samir: What's your typical warmup time?
13:40 Priya: Depends on model size and session, but our bench harness will show cache hit rates over time.
14:00 Jordan: On the SDK side — we recommend you try the openai-compat client we expose; if you prefer native Redwood SDK it'll have extra helpers for structured output and reranking.
14:20 Ben: For function calling, do you support nested function outputs? our schema can be nested.
14:30 Priya: Yes — function calling supports nested JSON, but we recommend validating server-side. sometimes transcription errors cause small malformations; we'll share parser utils.
15:00 Alicia: Timelines: can we aim for bench run week of April 6 and an initial results review by April 13?
15:15 Jordan: That aligns with 6-week plan. we'll aim to have bench scripts and security docs to you by April 2 so you can prep.
15:40 Ben: Any other dependencies? we may need a Redwood account and API key.
15:50 Jordan: We'll provision a POC API key and a sandbox project. that's part of the POC template I'll send.
16:10 Priya: A couple of notes on differences vs OpenAI — sometimes model variants have subtly different tokenization and function call heuristics; we'll run parity checks. Also quantization / model variant choices affect latency/cost tradeoffs.
16:45 Ben: Are there recommended model variants for low-latency extraction?
16:50 Priya: Lighter models with aggressive quantization typically perform better latency-wise. We can recommend a few and include performance profiles in the POC deck.
17:10 Samir: For private deployment, what's the deployment model? kube or dedicated appliance?
17:20 Jordan: Private can be either a VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed nodes or a Dedicated physical appliance in some cases; we'll tailor to your security needs. For POC we can do a hosted sandbox with VPC peering if that meets your rules.
17:50 Alicia: We'll check with security.
18:00 Ben: How do rollouts and fallbacks work? if a model is overloaded, can we fall back to a smaller model automatically?
18:10 Priya: Yes — routing policies can prefer low-latency region/model and fallback to a cheaper variant; you can set cost or latency preferences per route.
18:40 Jordan: Ok let's capture immediate next steps — I'll send the POC template and pricing, Priya will share bench harness and sample code, Ben will provide prompts and labeled data, Samir will confirm network constraints.
19:00 Alicia: One question — do you support function/tool calling to our internal APIs securely? we want to call our extraction microservice.
19:15 Priya: We support tool calling patterns; for private deployment we can enable secure internal endpoints via private connectivity. for hosted, you can proxy through a secure NAT with IP allowlists. We'll include recommended patterns.
19:45 Ben: For evaluation, we want both automatic metrics and a small human review to catch edge cases.
20:00 Jordan: Sounds good. we'll plan a 30-min check-in after bench results to go through metrics and next steps.
20:20 Alicia: Great. Any outstanding blockers?
20:30 Samir: I need to confirm that our infra team can allow the egress or peering; otherwise it's blocked.
20:45 Jordan: Understood — Samir if you can send the firewall constraints and timeline, Priya will advise the best path.
21:00 Ben: Also please share any sample prompt rate limits — we want to test burst shaping.
21:10 Priya: we'll include rate-limiting config examples in the repo.
21:30 Jordan: Ok wrapping up — recap: success criteria (p95 < 300ms short prompts, F1 > 0.9, cost target TBD), bench week of 4/6, security docs by 4/2, sample prompts by 4/3. next call to review bench results week of 4/13. I'll send calendar invites.
22:00 Alicia: Thanks everyone.
22:05 Ben: Thanks.
22:10 Samir: Thanks, bye.

Notes: transcription artifacts: 'red wood' occasionally transcribed as 'red wood' or 'Red-wood', 'K V cache' as 'K V cache', function calling sometimes shows as 'function slash tool calling'.

Shared artifacts mentioned: POC template (link to be sent), bench harness repo (github.com/redwood/poc-harness - placeholder), security pack (docs.redwood.com/security-poc), customer sample sheet (drive: /Meridian/benchmarks.xlsx).
